aliases: 2024 race for Michigan's other Senate seat

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed wins primary
evidence: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary in Michigan, CBS News projects, in a closely watched contest that represented the latest test of the party's divisions.

nary_nodes.label: Stevens drops out
evidence: a third candidate, state Sen. Mallory McMorrow, dropped out of the race last month.

nary_nodes.label: Stevens endorsed by Whitmer
evidence: securing an endorsement from outgoing popular Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer last month.

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed endorsed by progressives
evidence: secured the backing of prominent progressives like Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and independent Sen. Bernie Sanders in the primary

nary_nodes.label: Peters won't seek reelection
evidence: Democratic Sen. Gary Peters announced he wouldn't seek reelection, setting up a competitive race in the state.

nary_nodes.label: General election in November
evidence: With the primary victory, El-Sayed is set to take on former Rep. Mike Rogers in November.

nary_nodes.label: Rogers ran unopposed
evidence: Rogers ran unopposed in the Republican primary, after narrowly losing to Sen. Elissa Slotkin in the 2024 race for Michigan's other Senate seat, giving him months to home in on his general election pitch while Democrats' primary fight grew increasingly ugly.

nary_nodes.label: Synagogue attack in March
evidence: El-Sayed responded to March's attack on a Detroit-area synagogue by saying, in part, that "hurt people hurt people," he stood by what he said and reiterated his condemnation of the attack.

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed criticized for campaigning with Piker
evidence: while receiving criticism himself for campaigning with left-wing podcaster Hasan Piker.

nary_nodes.label: Stevens received pro-Israel funding
evidence: he hammered Stevens throughout the campaign for receiving an influx of funding from pro-Israel groups

nary_nodes.label: Insurgent Democrats win primaries
evidence: El-Sayed's victory comes after a series of primary wins by insurgent Democrats in places like New York City and Colorado in recent months, as progressives and democratic socialists seek changes to the party.

nary_nodes.label: Stevens warns against GOP
evidence: "Donald Trump and Mike Rogers want us to come out of this primary tired and divided, so their billionaire backers can come in and let multimillionaire Mike Rogers walk away with this Senate seat," Stevens said, while warning of the broader implications for the Senate should the GOP flip the seat. "I'm not going to let that happen."

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed calls for unity
evidence: "Whatever differences that we might have had in the primary, they pale in comparison to what unifies us: a recognition that so long as we want to keep our democracy, that democracy better be working for people, and that all of us have to come together to make sure that we never let Mike Rogers see the inside of the U.S. Senate," he said.

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed condemns attack
evidence: "I condemn the attack. It was a vile, antisemitic attack."

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed on Jewish safety
evidence: El-Sayed added that his commitment to Jewish safety is the same as his commitment to his children. "That's the highest commitment I can offer as a father," he said.

nary_nodes.label: El-Sayed on Michigan voters
evidence: Asked about the dynamic, El-Sayed told O'Keefe ahead of the primary that "it's always funny to me that people want to say that this state votes for moderates when it voted for Donald Trump twice." "It may just be that the better explanation is not that the state wants moderates, it's that it's so sick and tired of the establishment bought off by corporations on both sides of the political aisle, that it was willing to hold its nose and vote for Donald Trump twice," he added. "Now, what happens if the alternative to the bought-off establishment happens to be instead of a narcissistic, megalomaniacal billionaire, a doctor who rebuilds health departments to eliminate medical debt and put glasses on kids' faces? I'm willing to test that proposition."

nary_nodes.label: Democrats praise El-Sayed
evidence: Schumer and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, the chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, praised El-Sayed in a joint statement following his projected victory for running an "energetic campaign that inspired thousands of Michiganders across the state." "Democrats are united by a common purpose: putting a check on Donald Trump by defeating his Republican enablers and taking back the Senate," the Democrats said. "We look forward to working with Abdul and Democrats across Michigan to win this seat in November."
